newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
White sugar futures in London finished slightly lower in modest activity. By the close, March was 60 cents lower at $299.1 per tonne while March gave up 80 cents to close at $298.7 per tonne.
In New York raw sugar futures closed barely changed after eight days of falls. Even though a technical correction cannot be excluded, the overall picture remains dim.
A higher than expected European crop and record stocks are likely to stall any major recovery in spite of a satisfactory growth of world demand.
However, the low prices this year could well have an impact on the 1997/98 crop.
March ended 2 points higher at 10.51 cents/lb while May gave up 2 points to close at 10.60 cents/lb.

RUSSIA - Russia's plan to restrict white sugar imports through quotas could be in trouble as Boris Yeltsin's administration has apparently objected. The Foreign Trade Ministry last year sent an order to the government calling for white sugar imports to be set at 1.5 million tonnes a year, including 1.15 million tonnes from the Ukraine. It did not say when the quota, which must be approved by the government, would be introduced.

According to figures released by the Foreign Trade Ministry raw sugar imports in 1996 reached 1.60 million tonnes. According to Russia's Sugar Producers Union white sugar imports in the first ten months of 1996 reached 1.30 million tonnes, mostly from the Ukraine.

However, these figures do not reflect actual shipments as the export statistics of the country's trading partners show that imports in 1996, from countries other than the Ukraine, were at least 2.7 to 2.8 million tonnes.
The largest supplier apart from the Ukraine was Cuba. Other major suppliers were the EU, Brazil, India and Thailand.
If white sugar imports cannot be restricted by quotas it can be assumed that the government will use import tariffs to protect its sugar industry.
Russian Foreign Economic Relations Minister Oleg Davydov recently said that Moscow would use import tariffs to protect its domestic industries until they get back on their feet.

DOMINICAN REPUBLIC - Sugar production in March 1996 reached 79,288 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 92,619 tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first four months of 1995/96 (November/March) up to 253,826 tonnes compared to 245,525 tonnes in the like period the previous year.
Total production in 1994/95 hit a low of 482,404 tonnes, down from 627,779 tonnes in 1993/94 and 632,707 tonnes in 1992/93.

Sugar exports in March 1996 reached 37,765 tonnes, down from 59,785 tonnes in March 1995. This brought cumulative exports in November/March 1995/96 up to 70,304 tonnes, down from 91,870 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 263,380 tonnes against 314,545 tonnes in 1993/94.

TAIWAN - Sugar imports in October 1996 amounted to 31,503 tonnes, raw value, hardly changed from last year's 31,500 tonnes. This brought total imports in 1995/96 (November/October) up to 124,079 tonnes compared to 125,386 tonnes in 1994/95 and 32,747 tonnes in 1993/94.

The major country of origin in November/October 1995/96 was Australia with 124,000 tonnes raws against 124,878 tonnes in 1994/95. Sugar exports in 1995/96 amounted to 25,562 tonnes, up from 14,782 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in 1995/96 was the USA with 25,534 tonnes raws compared to 14,282 tonnes.
